title: 1 Publishing Method (GitHub Pages)
text:
This repository uses Quarto to render a documentation website to GitHub Pages.
We are adopting Option B: tag-based publishing to build release discipline ahead of 510(k) submission. Day-to-day edits can continue rapidly, but public publication is tied to explicit versioned releases.



Enable fast iteration on content without continuously changing the public site.
Ensure each public publication maps to a specific, immutable git state.
Maintain a clear, auditable workflow identifying who approved and who performed a release.
Provide practical ways for reviewers to preview changes before merging and before release.





Source: .qmd files and assets in this repository.
Rendered site: output written to _site/ by Quarto.
Release: a published website update that corresponds to a git tag (e.g. v0.3.0).
Approver(s): named individuals responsible for release approval.
Release manager: the person who creates the tag (or GitHub Release) and triggers publication.







The public GitHub Pages site should publish only from version tags on main, e.g.:

v0.1.0, v0.2.0, v1.0.0






Normal pushes to feature branches.
Normal merges/pushes to main that are not tagged.





A tag is an immutable pointer to a specific commit, making it easy to answer:

“What exact content is currently published?”
“Which changes are in the published documentation vs in-progress edits?”









Create a feature branch for each change set.
Keep PRs small when possible (one theme per PR).





Use Quarto’s preview server:

quarto preview

Use a full render to validate a clean build:

quarto render






Use PR review to gate changes into main.
Prefer requiring at least one reviewer for all PRs.





We need reviewers to preview changes before merging and before releasing.



Local preview (fastest for authors)

Authors run quarto preview while editing.
Good for rapid iteration, but not ideal as the only review mechanism.

PR build artifacts (recommended for reviewers)

CI renders the site for a PR and uploads _site/ as a downloadable artifact.
Reviewers download and open the generated HTML locally (or serve it locally).
Benefits:

Preview is reproducible (built in CI).
No need for reviewers to install Quarto/TinyTeX.


Main preview

main can be previewed the same way as PRs:

CI builds and attaches artifacts for commits.
Or a maintainer can run quarto preview locally.




Note: GitHub Pages itself is reserved for released tags, so it remains stable and clearly “official.”








PRs merged to main are reviewed and CI is green.
Any visible version string in the site (e.g., footer “Document Version”) is updated as appropriate.
Decide the next tag (semantic versioning recommended).





A release is approved by the designated approver(s) listed below.
Approval should be recorded in one of these forms:

A GitHub Issue/Discussion titled “Release vX.Y.Z approval” with explicit approval comments.
A PR that bumps the version, with required reviewers approving.






The release manager creates an annotated tag on the intended commit on main:

vX.Y.Z






GitHub Actions renders and deploys the site.
The published site now corresponds to vX.Y.Z.







Fill these in and keep them current.

Primary approver: TBD
Secondary approver (backup): TBD




Fill these in and keep them current.

Release manager(s): TBD





Add CODEOWNERS so specific files/sections require review.
Require branch protection on main:

required reviews
required status checks (Quarto render)

Add a short “release PR” that bumps the displayed document version and links the release tag.






Use semantic-ish versioning even during early development:

v0.MINOR.PATCH is fine for pre-1.0 work.

Tie the site-visible “Document Version” to the tag name whenever possible.





_site/ is build output and should not be hand-edited.
Stopping quarto preview with Ctrl-C results in a non-zero exit code (expected).

title: How to Contribute
text:
This documentation is designed to be easy to review and improve.
If you are a clinician or reviewer, you can contribute without installing any tools.

title: How to Contribute
section: 1 Option 1: Report an issue (recommended for feedback)
text:
1 Option 1: Report an issue (recommended for feedback)
On any page, use the Issue / Report an issue link.

This opens a GitHub Issue where you can describe the change you want.
This is best for requests, questions, or feedback that needs discussion.

title: How to Contribute
section: 2 Option 2: Suggest a direct edit in the browser
text:
2 Option 2: Suggest a direct edit in the browser
On any page, use the Edit link.
This will open the corresponding source file (a .qmd file) on GitHub.
Typical flow:

Click Edit.
Make a small change (typo fix, wording clarification, etc.).
GitHub will prompt you to create a new branch and open a Pull Request (PR).
Submit the PR.

A maintainer will review the PR and merge it when approved.

title: How to Contribute
text:
3 Option 3: Edit locally (for larger changes)
If you are comfortable with developer tools:

Clone the repository.
Edit .qmd files.
Preview locally with quarto preview.
Open a PR.

title: How to Contribute
text:
4 What happens after you contribute

Proposed changes are reviewed via Pull Requests.
The public website is published from version tags (e.g. v0.2.0) rather than every merge.

title: How to Contribute
text:
5 Tips for making good edits

Keep changes small and focused.
Prefer plain language.
For IFU/safety content: keep wording unambiguous and consistent.

title: Intended Use
text:
The OralEye Oral Imaging System is a portable, non-invasive imaging device designed for capturing high-resolution intraoral images using visible and fluorescence imaging modalities.



The OralEye system is intended for:

Capturing intraoral photographs for diagnostic purposes
Documenting oral conditions and treatment progress
Patient education and communication
Integration with digital patient records





Age Range: All ages
Conditions: General oral health screening and documentation
Contraindications: None known





Enhanced visualization of oral structures
Improved patient communication
Comprehensive documentation
Support for treatment planning




The device is indicated for use in dental practice settings for capturing and storing intraoral images to assist in:

Clinical examination
Diagnosis and treatment planning
Patient record documentation
Patient education




There are no known contraindications for use of this device when used as directed.









Warning




This device is prescription-use only and should be operated by trained dental professionals
Not intended for use as the sole basis for diagnosis
Images should be interpreted by qualified dental professionals







Type: Intraoral camera system
Modalities:

Visible light reflectance imaging
Fluorescence imaging

Portability: Handheld, battery-operated


For complete safety information, see Safety Information

title: Safety Information
text:
Critical Safety Information



Read and understand all safety information before using the OralEye system. Failure to follow these instructions may result in injury or device damage.








Use only the provided power adapter
Do not expose the device to liquids
Disconnect power before cleaning
Do not use if power cord is damaged





Ensure patient comfort during imaging procedures
Avoid prolonged LED exposure to eyes
Use appropriate infection control procedures
Follow standard precautions for patient contact





LED light source is safe for intended use
Do not stare directly into LED array
Automatic exposure control prevents overexposure








Barrier Protection: Use disposable barriers for intraoral components
Surface Disinfection: Clean all surfaces with approved disinfectant after each patient
Hand Hygiene: Follow standard hand hygiene protocols





Isopropyl alcohol (70%)
EPA-registered hospital-grade disinfectants
Follow manufacturer’s contact time recommendations







Warning



Do not autoclave or immerse device in liquid. Do not use abrasive cleaners.









Temperature: 15°C to 30°C (59°F to 86°F)
Humidity: 30% to 75% relative humidity
Pressure: 700 hPa to 1060 hPa





Temperature: -10°C to 50°C (14°F to 122°F)
Humidity: 10% to 90% relative humidity (non-condensing)








Do not dispose of device in regular waste
Follow local regulations for electronic waste disposal
Contact manufacturer for recycling options





Lithium-ion batteries must be recycled according to local regulations
Contact local waste management for battery recycling





Report adverse events or device problems to:

Manufacturer: support@oraleye.ai
FDA: via MedWatch (1-800-FDA-1088)


This safety information is current as of the document effective date.
